cards.statement: The kubelet exposes node resource metrics through its `/metrics/resource` endpoint.
cards.explanation: The endpoint publishes summarized node resource statistics for the resource metrics pipeline.

cards.statement: The kubelet uses a separate cAdvisor Deployment to collect container resource metrics.
cards.explanation: cAdvisor collection code is included in the kubelet; it needs no separate Deployment.
cards.misconception: The kubelet depends on a separately deployed cAdvisor service.

cards.statement: With metrics-server installed, kube-apiserver can serve the Metrics API through the API aggregation layer.
cards.explanation: Registering the Metrics API as an APIService routes resource metric requests to metrics-server.

cards.statement: With metrics-server installed, it restores resource metric history from disk after a Pod restart.
cards.explanation: metrics-server keeps short-term metrics in memory; restarting its Pod loses that state.
cards.misconception: metrics-server persists resource metrics for recovery after restarts.

cards.statement: With metrics-server installed, its resource Metrics API can report Pod filesystem usage.
cards.explanation: The resource Metrics API exposes CPU and memory usage; filesystem usage needs a fuller monitoring pipeline.
cards.misconception: The resource Metrics API includes filesystem usage.

cards.statement: kube-scheduler uses live CPU usage to decide whether a node has room for another Pod.
cards.explanation: kube-scheduler accounts for CPU requests. Low measured CPU usage does not free CPU already committed through requests.
cards.misconception: kube-scheduler finds available CPU from measured usage rather than requests.

source.title: Resource Management for Pods and Containers

cards.statement: The kubelet subtracts `kubeReserved` from node capacity to calculate allocatable resources.
cards.explanation: Resources reserved for Kubernetes system daemons reduce the amount available to scheduled Pods.

source.title: Reserve Compute Resources for System Daemons

cards.statement: The kubelet reserves hard-eviction memory headroom when calculating Node Allocatable.
cards.explanation: Memory reserved through `evictionHard` stays outside the Pod resource budget, even if system daemons reserve nothing.

source.title: Reserve Compute Resources for System Daemons

cards.statement: kube-apiserver publishes its system metrics in Prometheus format for monitoring scrapers.
cards.explanation: Monitoring systems scrape this text format to build component dashboards and alerts.

cards.statement: A scraper reads kube-scheduler's internal metrics from kube-apiserver's `/metrics` endpoint.
cards.explanation: Scrape kube-scheduler's own `/metrics` endpoint for its internal metrics.
cards.misconception: kube-apiserver centrally exposes other control plane components' internal metrics.

cards.statement: The container runtime sends application stdout and stderr to the node's systemd journal.
cards.explanation: Container output uses CRI log files; the runtime's own logs use journald.
cards.misconception: Container logs use journald.

cards.statement: The kubelet's `podLogsDir` setting lets administrators choose a directory other than `/var/log/pods`.
cards.explanation: Set `podLogsDir` in KubeletConfiguration to relocate Pod container logs.

cards.statement: The container runtime rotates logs using its own `containerLogMaxSize` setting.
cards.explanation: `containerLogMaxSize` configures the kubelet's container log rotation.
cards.misconception: The runtime owns the container log rotation configuration.

cards.statement: The kubelet reads the container log file when handling a `kubectl logs` request.
cards.explanation: The kubelet returns local log file contents through the API.

cards.statement: `kubectl logs` returns retained rotated files along with the latest container log file.
cards.explanation: `kubectl logs` returns the latest file, excluding retained older files.
cards.misconception: kubectl logs includes rotated files.

cards.statement: By default, the kubelet erases a container's previous logs when that container restarts.
cards.explanation: The kubelet retains the preceding container's logs after a restart.
cards.misconception: Restarts erase previous container logs.

cards.statement: By default, the kubelet removes a Pod's container logs from the node when it evicts the Pod.
cards.explanation: Eviction removes Pod containers and their local logs.

cards.statement: The Kubernetes documentation recommends a DaemonSet for a node-level logging agent.
cards.explanation: Node-level agents collect local container files across cluster nodes.

cards.statement: With a sidecar logging agent forwarding to a backend instead of stdout, `kubectl logs` can read its collected logs.
cards.explanation: Retrieve a sidecar logging agent's forwarded application logs from its backend.
cards.misconception: Backend records appear in kubectl logs.

cards.statement: Raising kube-apiserver's log verbosity exposes detailed request traces in its output.
cards.explanation: Higher verbosity adds detailed events that help an administrator investigate kube-apiserver behavior.

cards.statement: By default, kubeadm init deploys kube-proxy as a systemd service for the cluster's Linux nodes.
cards.explanation: kubeadm init installs kube-proxy through the API server as a DaemonSet. Inspect that workload to locate its Pods.
cards.misconception: kubeadm installs kube-proxy as a host systemd service.

cards.statement: An administrator checks kube-proxy's startup logs to identify the active Service proxy mode on a failing node.
cards.explanation: kube-proxy reports its selected proxy mode in startup logs, helping an administrator choose the appropriate node-level checks.

cards.statement: In iptables mode, kube-proxy installs Service forwarding rules in the kernel of each node in the cluster.
cards.explanation: Inspect the rules on the affected node when debugging Service forwarding. kube-proxy synchronizes its node's rules with cluster state.

cards.statement: Before the Pod network add-on is installed, Pending CoreDNS Pods indicate a failed kubeadm initialization.
cards.explanation: Pending CoreDNS Pods are expected before the administrator installs a Pod network add-on. They can be part of a successful kubeadm initialization.
cards.misconception: Pending CoreDNS Pods before network installation mean cluster initialization failed.

cards.statement: With the log plugin's default configuration, CoreDNS records received DNS queries even when they succeed.
cards.explanation: The CoreDNS log plugin makes received queries visible during DNS troubleshooting, including successful lookups.

cards.statement: An administrator inspects the DNS Service's EndpointSlices to check the DNS server addresses it exposes.
cards.explanation: The DNS Service's EndpointSlices list backend server addresses for checking whether Service forwarding has a destination.

cards.statement: CoreDNS can keep Service DNS records current when RBAC grants get instead of list and watch.
cards.explanation: CoreDNS needs list and watch permissions on Services and EndpointSlices to discover records and follow their changes.
cards.misconception: get permission replaces the list and watch permissions CoreDNS needs.

cards.statement: An administrator fixes CoreDNS forwarding loops by pointing kubelet's resolv-conf at a systemd-resolved stub.
cards.explanation: Point kubelet's resolv-conf at /run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf to supply upstream resolvers. The stub can create a forwarding loop.
cards.misconception: The systemd-resolved stub file supplies suitable upstream DNS configuration.

cards.statement: An administrator prevents Pod routing conflicts by placing the Pod network range inside the host network range.
cards.explanation: Keep Pod network ranges separate from host networks. Overlapping ranges can break routing.
cards.misconception: Nesting the Pod network inside the host network avoids routing conflicts.

cards.statement: With a plugin that enforces NetworkPolicy, a policy can block traffic to a healthy Service backend.
cards.explanation: A healthy backend can still be unreachable because a NetworkPolicy restricts traffic to its Pod. Review the policies during network troubleshooting.

cards.statement: A DaemonSet using OnDelete replaces its existing Pods when an administrator changes the Pod template.
cards.explanation: With OnDelete, the DaemonSet controller waits for an administrator to delete an existing Pod before replacing it with the changed template.
cards.misconception: OnDelete applies template changes to existing Pods immediately.

source.title: Perform a Rolling Update on a DaemonSet

cards.statement: With RollingUpdate, a StatefulSet's partition lets the controller update Pods at or above that ordinal.
cards.explanation: During a partitioned StatefulSet rollout, Pods below the partition retain the earlier template.

cards.statement: With Secret encryption configured, kube-apiserver uses the first listed provider for new Secret writes.
cards.explanation: Provider order in EncryptionConfiguration determines how kube-apiserver stores new Secret writes.

cards.statement: When an administrator enables Secret encryption, kube-apiserver also rewrites previously stored Secrets.
cards.explanation: Existing Secrets keep their stored representation until rewritten. An administrator can use kubectl replace to apply the new encryption configuration.
cards.misconception: Changing the encryption configuration migrates existing Secrets automatically.

cards.statement: The HorizontalPodAutoscaler controller runs within the kube-controller-manager process.
cards.explanation: The kube-controller-manager process hosts the controller that reconciles HorizontalPodAutoscaler objects.

cards.statement: The HPA can compute CPU utilization from usage when a target Pod's CPU requests are unset.
cards.explanation: The HPA needs CPU requests to compute utilization. Missing requests leave utilization undefined for that metric.
cards.misconception: Measured CPU usage alone is enough to calculate HPA utilization.

cards.statement: With multiple working metrics, an HPA chooses the largest replica count proposed by those metrics.
cards.explanation: The HPA evaluates metrics separately and selects the greatest proposed replica count, subject to its configured bounds.

cards.statement: Since Kubernetes v1.30, an HPA's ContainerResource metric automatically follows a container through a name change.
cards.explanation: ContainerResource selects a container by its configured name. An administrator updates the HPA when renaming that container.
cards.misconception: ContainerResource tracks container identity across renames.

cards.statement: The HPA's scale-down stabilization uses the highest replica recommendation in its configured window.
cards.explanation: Scale-down stabilization considers recent recommendations to prevent a brief drop in demand from immediately removing replicas.

cards.statement: kubeadm init installs the VerticalPodAutoscaler controller as a standard cluster add-on.
cards.explanation: VerticalPodAutoscaler is a separate add-on that an administrator installs in the cluster.
cards.misconception: kubeadm includes VerticalPodAutoscaler in its standard add-ons.
